messages:
Jules (customer): Hey team — customer says a bunch of engineers kept access after we thought SCIM deprovisioned them. They renamed an Okta group from `eng-backend` → `engineering-backend` and expected role removal.
Maya (CSE): Which org? can you paste a user id and the group id?
Jules (customer): org: 5621, example user: u_0a1b2c3d, group id: g-9f8e7d6c
Maya (CSE): Thanks. I see our SCIM logs show a PATCH from Okta with the new group name and member list. scim-bot, can you dump the last 3 provisioning events for g-9f8e7d6c?
scim-bot: 
```
1732109876 PATCH /scim/v2/Groups/g-9f8e7d6c 200 OK
payload: {"displayName":"engineering-backend","members":[{"value":"u_0a1b2c3d"}, {"value":"u_4d5e6f7g"}]}
processed: enqueue role_sync job for group g-9f8e7d6c
1732109882 role_sync: started job group=g-9f8e7d6c
1732109883 role_sync: warn "token_missing_scope" operation=remove_role required=["users:write"] token_scopes=["scim:read","groups:write"]
1732109883 role_sync: skipped remove_role for u_0a1b2c3d (retained role anchor=eng-backend)
1732109884 role_sync: completed (partial)
```
Aman (eng): That log is the important bit — the SCIM token used by the customer's Okta push or our connector doesn't include the `users:write` scope, so our role-removal path bails out. The group rename makes our displayName-based mapping miss, so the role anchor on the user stays `eng-backend` and we don't remove the role.
Priya (SRE): TL;DR — two simultaneous bugs: 1) mapping relies on `displayName` (mutable) instead of stable id/externalId. 2) token scopes for provisioning were changed during a recent token rotation (or customer misconfigured Okta) and missing `users:write` so remove ops are ignored.
Maya (CSE): Customer insists they sent the group deletion for that user — but the payload had the new displayName not matching our mapping so we didn't reconcile. Can we give a remediation and a safe repro?
Aman (eng): Repro steps:
1) Create Okta group `eng-backend` mapped to SCIM group externalId `ext-g-123`
2) Provision users uA, uB
3) Rename group to `engineering-backend` in Okta (Okta sends PATCH with new displayName)
4) Okta Push uses a token w/o `users:write` scope
Expected: users in that group have role removed. Actual: SCIM endpoint returns 200 and job runs, but remove_role is skipped due to insufficient scope; role anchor still `eng-backend` so app keeps role.
Workaround (short-term):
- Ask customer to include `users:write` in the Okta SCIM token scopes; re-trigger a full group sync (Okta Push > Re-provision)
- OR run our admin backfill: `scripts/scim_reconcile.py --org 5621 --group-id g-9f8e7d6c --force-remove` (requires admin creds)
Permanent fixes (engineering):
- Prefer `externalId` or immutable group id for role mapping instead of displayName.
- Make role_removal tolerant: if externalId doesn't match, diff member lists and remove roles for users no longer in the group.
- Fail provisioning job on missing token scopes (make it return a 4xx to Okta instead of pretending success) so customer sees the error.
Priya (SRE): I'll draft an incident note for the runbook: if `role_sync` sees `token_missing_scope` then:
- surface a visible error to the SCIM audit log
- attach a remediation link in the console
- generate an automatic ticket to CSE if group had > 1 member and partial completion
Maya (CSE): I'll message the customer with steps: rotate Okta token to include `users:write`, then trigger a re-provision for the affected group OR let us run the backfill.
Jules (customer): Thanks. If you can run the backfill that'd be ideal — they have compliance requirements.
Aman (eng): I'll open a PR with two small changes: map by `externalId` when present, and make the role_sync job error when `users:write` isn't present (instead of warning). Also adding a reconciliation endpoint `/admin/scim/reconcile` that can be called by CSE.
Maya (CSE): ETA for PR to staging?
Aman (eng): EOD for a small flag change; full tests + staging by tomorrow morning.
Jules (customer): :thumbsup: appreciate the quick turnaround.
Maya (CSE): Will follow up once backfill completes. tagging @Priya (SRE) for audit log change.
Priya (SRE): noted — will file change request.
scim-bot: ticket created: #SCIM-5621-role-reconcile
